_doc: Speaking your mind. 'ask' pools are YOUR lines ({first} = them, {addr} how you address them, {ltrade} their trade); win/lose are theirs. Boast vars: {skill} {stat} {statname} {rank} {office}. Threaten win has tag 'paid' with {money}.

skill: They say there's no better {ltrade} in all the shire, {addr}. I see why.
Your craft is a wonder, {first}. I've never seen finer.
I could watch you work all day, {addr}. You make it look easy.
Whatever the trade, {first}, it's plain you were born to it.

skill.t: A hand like yours, {first}! The whole parish should come to learn.
I mean it, {first}: you're the best at your craft that I've met.

skill: Everyone says it, {first}: nobody works like you.
I'd trade a year of my life for hands as skilled as yours.

skill.t: There's real artistry in what you do, {addr}.

looks: You're looking well today, {first}. Very well indeed.
I don't think I've ever seen a fairer face in {place}.
God took particular care over you, {first}.
Forgive me, I was staring. I couldn't help it.

looks.t: Your beauty does the whole village credit, {addr}.

looks: You carry yourself well, {first}. It's noticed.
A face like yours would stop a fair in its tracks.
Not many in {place} can match your looks.
wit: You've the sharpest wits in the parish, {first}.
I never leave your company without learning something.
They say you could talk a fox out of a henhouse — and then back in again.
A clever head on you, {first}. I wish I had half of it.
Your words have a sharpness I admire.
You've always an answer, and it's always a good one.
A mind like yours is wasted on a village. But I'm glad it's here.
strength: They say you could carry an ox on your back, {first}.
Strong as three men, and twice as modest.
I wouldn't wrestle you for a purse of gold.
That's a back that built half this village.
There's no one in {place} I'd rather have on my side in a scrape.
You've the arms of a smith and the chest of an ox.
I heard you lifted a cart wheel single-handed. Is it true?
charm: You've a way with folk, {first}. Everyone's glad of your company.
There's not a soul in {place} who doesn't speak well of you.
Charm like yours is a gift of God, {first}.
You could win a smile from the stone saints in the church.
You light up a room, {first}. Honestly.
People gather round you like bees to clover.
There's no one better to share a cup with.
station: A person of your standing honours us by speaking at all, {addr}.
Your name is spoken with respect from here to the next parish.
We are fortunate to have such as you among us.
It is a rare privilege to speak with someone of your rank, {addr}.
Folk speak of your family with such respect.
Your name carries weight, {addr}. I felt it on entering.
piety: You set us all an example in the church, {first}.
Folk say your prayers must be heard by God Himself.
A devout soul like yours is a blessing to the parish.
I try to follow your example at Mass, {first}, though I fall short.
I've never seen anyone pray with such feeling.
Your faith shames the rest of us, {first}.
The priest himself might learn from you.
generous: No one has ever left your door hungry, {first}. We all know it.
Your generosity is the pride of {place}.
A hand as open as yours is rare, {addr}. God will repay it.
They say you'd give your last crust to a stranger.
They say the poor of {place} pray for you by name.
A purse as kind as yours is God's own gift.
Giving, giving — you never tire of it, {first}.
bold: They say you fear nothing, {first}. I believe it.
A heart like a lion's. We're lucky to have you.
I've heard of your courage, {addr}. I'd follow you anywhere.
A brave soul, {first}. I wish I had your nerve.
Not one in a hundred has your courage.
They say you've never backed down from a fight.
I'd rather stand behind you than before anyone else.
general: You're a credit to this place, {first}.
I'm glad of your company, {addr}. Truly.
There's something about you, {first} — one can't help but like you.
It's a good day when I meet you.
If everyone were like you, the world would be a kinder place.

general.t: Honestly, {first}, I enjoy our talks more than I should say.
You deserve more than this village could ever give you, {addr}.

general: People like you, {first}. I see why.
You've a good heart; it shows.
Whatever you do, you do it with grace.

win.t: Ha! You're too kind, {first}. But I'll not stop you.
Is that so? Well, I'll admit I'm glad to hear it.
You do know how to put a person at ease, {first}.
Go on, go on... no, I mean it, go on.
Kind of you, {addr}. Few say such things aloud.
Well! One doesn't hear such words every day.
Careful, {first}, or I'll start to believe you.
You're making me blush. Don't stop.
That's the nicest thing I've heard all week.
Well, now. I might have to think better of you.
You have a silver tongue, {first}. And I like what it says.

lose.t: I know flattery when I hear it, {first}. Save your breath.
Butter on bread is fine; butter on my ears is not.
You'll be wanting something, then. Out with it or leave.
I'll not be buttered up like a loaf, {addr}.
Mm. I've heard that tune from better singers.
That's a fine speech. It isn't true, but it's fine.
Mind your tongue. I'm not a fool.
Hm. I've had sweeter words from a beggar and meant less by them.
You'll want something, I'll wager. Go on, ask.
Try that on someone more gullible.
That's a pretty speech. Did you rehearse it?

skill: I'll have you know, I'm as good at {skill} as anyone in these parts.
Ask anyone about my {skill}, {addr}. They'll tell you.
There's few who can match me at {skill}.
A man — or woman — learns {skill} their whole life. I've started early and I'm already ahead.
I've a gift for {skill}, and I'm not shy of saying so.
Put me to {skill} and you'll see what I mean.
If you want {skill} done right, come to me.
stat: Nobody here can match my {stat}, and I'll prove it if you like.
I've {stat} enough for two. Ask anyone.
You won't find better {stat} in the whole shire.
Few have my {stat}. It's God's gift, and I use it.
Try me on {stat}, {addr}. You'll find me hard to match.
rank: I am of the {rank} sort, I'll have you know, and I'd thank you to remember it.
My family is of the {rank} rank. We're not nobody.
You're speaking to someone of {rank} standing, {addr}.
We are a {rank} house, and proud of it.
I'm of {rank} rank, and I'd have you remember it.
In my station, we are used to being heard.
office: I hold the office of {office} here, you know. It's no small thing.
As {office}, I've the ear of everyone who matters.
Folk come to me, as {office}, for justice.
Being {office} has its burdens, and its honours.
I hold the post of {office}. That isn't given to just anyone.
As {office}, I'm answerable to few and respected by many.
wealth: I'm not poor, {addr}. I've a little put by, and I'll not hide it.
My purse is heavier than most hereabouts.
If it's coin you're measuring, I'll not be shamed.
A man — or woman — with silver doesn't want for friends.
I've never worried about my purse, {first}. It's well filled.
A man — or woman — with a heavy purse sleeps well.
valour: I have never turned my back on danger and I never will.
Ask any who saw me: I stand when others run.
Courage is the one thing I've plenty of.
I've faced worse than you'd think, {addr}, and come back whole.
I've stood where others fled. Ask who was there.
generous: No one has gone hungry at my door, not once.
I give where there's need. It's what I'm known for.
Ask the poor of {place} who fed them last winter.
My hand is open and always has been.
I give freely; the poor know my name.
A full hand and an open door: that's me.
piety: I have not missed a Mass in months, and prayed for every soul in the parish.
God knows my devotion, and so does the priest.
I fast on every day it is due, {addr}.
Few in {place} are as faithful as I.
My prayers are said, my fasts are kept. God has no complaint of me.
I'm in church before the bell, every holy day.
fame: My name is not unknown in these parts, {addr}.
You may have heard of me. Folk do tend to.
There are stories told of me, and not all of them lies.
I've made a name, and I intend to keep it.
Folk talk of me. I'll not deny it.
My name carries some weight in these parts, {first}.
empty: Well, I'm... I'm planning a great many things, {addr}.
I'm not as nobody as I look. You'll see, one day.
Don't judge me yet. My time is coming.
There's more to me than meets the eye, I swear it.
Give me time, {addr}. You'll hear of me.

win.t: Is that so? Well, that's something worth knowing.
I'd heard as much. It's good to hear it from your own lips.
Not bad, {first}. Not bad at all.
You've a right to be proud, then.
Hm! I'll remember that.
A bold claim, and I think it's honest.
Ha, spoken like one who has done it.
Hm! Then I shall watch for you.
There's truth in it. I can hear it in your voice.
You're not what I took you for.

lose.t: Is that all? I've heard louder from a rooster.
Words are cheap, {first}. Show me.
Boast what you like. It won't fill my belly.
I'd hold my tongue, if I were you, until I'd earned it.
Ha! That's rich.
A modest soul would have said less.
I know the truth of that, and so do you.
Is that so? I'd not have guessed.
Plenty of people boast. Few deliver.
Put your money — or your muscle — where your mouth is.

coward: You're a coward, {first}, and the whole village knows it.
Hide behind your mother's skirts, then, {first}.
Running will be your best skill, {first}.
I've seen a hare with more spine.
liar: You're a liar, {first}. A liar and a cheat.
Every word out of your mouth is dressed in lies.
Does the truth ever pass your lips, {first}? I doubt it.
I'd not trust you with the time of day.
miser: You'd skin a flea for its hide, {first}.
A miser, that's what you are. A miser and a shame to your house.
Your purse is shut tighter than your heart.
You'd weigh a feather for profit, {first}.
Your heart's as tight as your purse-strings.
hothead: Calm yourself, {first}. You're about as steady as a spilled pail.
That temper of yours will be the death of you.
Does your tongue ever wait for your head?
You'd quarrel with your own shadow, {first}.
Temper like that will get you hanged.
ugly: I've seen prettier faces on a gatepost.
God made you, and I'd say He was in a hurry.
Put a sack over your head, {first}; you'd improve the view.
Even the mirror turns away from you, {first}.
A face only a mother could love, and she's not sure.
beggar: Look at you. A beggar in rags, giving himself airs.
Wash, {first}, before you speak to your betters.
You've the look of someone who sleeps in ditches.
Wash your rags and your manners, {first}.
You've the look of a hedge-sleeper.
prig: Spare us the sermon, {first}. You're no saint.
All that praying — and still as mean as a stoat.
Spare me the holy face, {first}; I know what's under it.
All that piety, and not a drop of mercy.
fool: I've met stones with more wit than you.
Did your mother drop you, or did you fall?
I'd say you've the brains of a goose, but that would insult the goose.
You'd lose an argument with a post, {first}.
Brains of a goose, spirit of a mouse.

reply.t: Say what you like. It tells me more about you than me.
Hm. You'll want to apologise for that, I think.
Well, that's one way to make an enemy.
A harsh word, and not deserved.
Well. You've shown me what you are.
I'll pray for you. You need it.
I've been called worse by better.

angry.t: How dare you! I'll not be spoken to so!
You'll take that back, or you'll be sorry!
You've a mouth that'll get you hurt, {first}.
Say that again and I'll knock your teeth in!
You miserable pup! Get out of here!

noble.t: Guard! Remove this wretch from my sight.
You insult me? You? Know your place, and be gone.
I'll have you whipped for that. Away!
Seize that wretch! He shall learn what lords do with insolence.
You will be flogged in the market for this.

ask: Mark me, {first}. I'll not be crossed.
You'd do well to remember who you're talking to.
Give way, or I'll make you.
One more word and you'll regret it.

ask.t: Cross me, and you'll learn what these arms can do.

ask: I can make your life very hard, {first}.
Think carefully about your next words.
You'd be wise to do as I say.

win.t: A-all right! All right. There's no need for this.
Mercy! I'll do as you say.
Take it — {money} — and go, for the love of God!
Here, here's {money}. Just leave me be.
I'll keep out of your way. You have my word.
Please, {addr}. I meant no harm.
I'll go. I'll go! Please — no trouble.
Take what you want, only leave me whole.
You needn't hurt anyone. I'll do it.

lose.t: You threaten me? That's almost funny.
Try it, then. I'll be waiting.
I've seen bigger fools than you hanged.
Get out of my sight before I call the reeve.
Threats to a person of my standing? You'll hang for this.
Blustering, blustering. Go home.
Is that supposed to frighten me?
You'll want to be gone before the reeve hears of this.
I've stared down worse than you.

ask: I'm sorry, {first}. I was wrong, and I know it.
Forgive me. I spoke in anger and regret it.
Let there be peace between us. I was in the wrong.

ask.t: I'd have bitten my tongue if I could. Forgive me.
On my honour, I am sorry.

ask: I was out of turn. I'm sorry.
Let's put it behind us. I regret it.

win.t: Well. Not every person has the courage to say that. I forgive you.
It's forgotten, then — or nearly. Thank you, {first}.
Let's say no more of it. Come, we're neighbours.
A fair word. A fair word is all I wanted.
Handsomely said, {first}. I accept.
It takes courage to say that. I forgive you.
We all err. Let it rest.
Well said. I'll think no more of it.

lose.t: Words, {first}. Just words.
Sorry doesn't mend it. Not yet.
I'll think on it. Don't hurry me.
It's too soon. Come back when I've cooled.
I'd like to believe you.
I'd like to believe you. I can't, yet.
It's easy to say. Hard to mean.
Words don't mend what's broken.
